label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/snapbug.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_longjump.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, B, C where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief asks for a 55-gallon drum, a cylinder with a round outline from above and below. The asset is a rectangular box. In the TOP and BELOW views (sides.png) the outline is a square, not a circle, and in the four angle views (FRONT-LEFT to BACK-RIGHT) the body is a block with four flat faces and hard vertical edges. The outline differs in shape, not only in paint, so this is a shape fault.

M2.reason: Measured 23 x 23 x 34, against the brief's 34 high and 23 across: 0% off, within 15%. This is only the bounding box; the form inside it is wrong (see M1 and M3).

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: the round body (a cylinder, the asset has four sides instead); the top and bottom chime rings (none in any view); the two bung plugs on the top (none in TOP or the angle views); the hazard stripe, which is painted and so counts only if its paint is there (none in any view); the rust, which is paint too. Missing: rings, bungs, stripe. The body's wrong form is also a fault.

M4.reason: Each view shows one flat mid-grey with a mottled noise texture, the same on all faces. The brief's painted steel body with rust reads as grey steel only in part; the rust (orange-brown wear) is absent everywhere, and the yellow and black hazard stripe is absent in all ten views. Clearly off, not the same material.

M5.reason: The surface markings the brief asks for are absent: no hazard stripe in any of the ten views, no rust patches, no panel or chime lines. Only a generic mottled noise, which reads as concrete, not as rusted steel.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the amendment directs, since the line-up test caps M6 and the measured result was not a double pick (caught once in four readings). Note for the record: the asset is visibly a plain grey box beside the Valve props in lineup.png, and a player who knows a drum would not take it for one. The 2 here is the measure's result, not a visual pass; the decoy-must-fail rule should be read against the other items, which fail it.

M7.reason: The box is upright and stands on its base, as a drum does. But the drum's front is marked by its bung plugs and the stripe's placement, and neither is there, so there is no front to check the orientation against.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty; SMAK's check passes. 12 triangles against a median of 99 for Half-Life's own of its kind, well under twice. Nothing open, inside out, or floating: a closed, sound box.
